bull.b: The move from deeply negative historical profitability to roughly 19% operating and 12.5% net margins shows meaningful operating leverage. Sustaining these levels would strengthen internally funded growth and debt-service capacity.

Higher dues, improved membership mix and growing personal training and spa activity demonstrate pricing power and deeper member monetization. These recurring and ancillary revenue streams can support durable revenue and margin growth beyond simple membership additions.

The planned club pipeline expands Life Time’s recurring membership platform, while refinancing lowers the cost of its sizable term loan through 2031. Together, growth capacity and reduced interest expense can improve long-term earnings and financial flexibility.

bear.b: Although leverage improved from 2025, debt remains high for a leisure business. A material debt burden can constrain investment choices, increase sensitivity to refinancing conditions and reduce resilience if membership demand weakens.

bear.t: Negative free cash flow and high capex
bear.b: Strong operating cash flow is being absorbed by club construction and expansion spending, leaving negative free cash flow. Continued investment may support growth, but it increases reliance on financing and sale-leasebacks to fund development.

Reported membership growth is modest and is being reduced further by the intentional removal of lower-paying qualified medical members. The mix strategy may improve dues, but slower volume growth places more pressure on pricing and ancillary spending.
